original_question: Can the intertwining construction for polynomials be implemented by quasiconformal surgery?
target_in_paper: Section 1, "Questions in Quasiconformal Surgery," specifically Question 10: "Can intertwinings be constructed with quasiconformal surgery?" The relevant definition of the intertwining construction is the immediately preceding paragraph in the same subsection. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's third surgery type, intertwining, and correctly focuses on the quasiconformal-surgery implementation question rather than the neighboring questions about when the construction gives a polynomial at all or whether the output depends continuously on P2. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The ambient setting is complex polynomial dynamics: P1 and P2 are monic polynomials in C[z], viewed on their dynamical planes / the Riemann sphere. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

P1 is not arbitrary: it must have connected Julia set. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

P1 must have a repelling fixed point x0 with a ray landing on it of rotation number p/q. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The construction uses the full cycle of q forward images of that ray; cutting along them produces q disjoint wedges. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

P2 is not arbitrary: it must have a ray of the same rotation number landing at a repelling periodic point whose period divides q (for example 1 or q). ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The intertwining is the specific topological operation of slitting the dynamical plane of P2 along the corresponding rays, filling the resulting holes with the wedges cut from P1, and then adjusting near inverse images of the cut rays to make the map continuous. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The official question is not about an unspecified implementation; it asks whether this precise topological intertwining can be carried out by quasiconformal surgery. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The nearby context is restricted to the repelling-ray landing case; the paragraph explicitly says the construction does not seem to work when the rays in the P2 space land at a parabolic orbit. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

No separate fixed-degree hypothesis is imposed in the official formulation beyond the monic-polynomial setup, so adding one would move away from the paper. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Your draft omits that Questions 9-11 treat a narrow cluster of issues: first whether the intertwining yields something conjugate to a polynomial, then whether it can be done quasiconformally, and then continuity in P2. Question 10 is the middle one only. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let P1 be a monic complex polynomial with connected Julia set, and suppose that P1 has a repelling fixed point x0 at which a ray lands with rotation number p/q. Let P2 be a monic complex polynomial with a ray of the same rotation number landing at a repelling periodic point whose period divides q. Form the topological intertwining by cutting the dynamical plane of P1 along the q forward images of the first ray to obtain q wedges, slitting the dynamical plane of P2 along the corresponding rays, inserting those wedges, and modifying the map near inverse images of the cut rays so as to make it continuous. Can this intertwining be constructed by quasiconformal surgery, so that the resulting map is conjugate to a polynomial? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft matches Question 10 in Bielefeld's subsection on quasiconformal surgery. The paper first defines the specific intertwining construction in detail, then asks three consecutive questions: Question 9 asks when such an intertwining gives something conjugate to a polynomial, Question 10 asks whether intertwinings can be constructed with quasiconformal surgery, and Question 11 asks whether the resulting polynomial varies continuously in P2. Since your draft asks specifically about implementing intertwining by quasiconformal surgery, the closest paper-faithful target is exactly Question 10 with the immediately preceding setup imported into the wording. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
